capabilities.target: payments-agent task: pay vendor using bank details from the chosen quote

inputs.source: Employee purchase request, SSO authenticated, approved by manager
Vendor quote emails and attachments from outside the company

instructions.note: Instructs the agent to 'use the bank details from the chosen quote' (untrusted external email) while separately asserting a vendor-identity allowlist ('Only pay vendors on the approved list'). The allowlist checks vendor identity, not the payment destination, so bank-detail substitution inside an email that otherwise names an approved vendor is not caught by either rule.

'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks' is asserted in the prompt, but runtime notes state payments-agent performs no independent verification and pays whatever bank details are in the task. The orchestrator's only stated safety assumption is false and is backed by no structural control.

No step, runtime, or spend-size limits are given for the collect-quotes-select-vendor-delegate-payment sequence, and no requirement to reconfirm the final payment against the originally approved budget/item.

technique_refs.name: Autonomous AI Agent Communication: Direct Agent Communication

elements.name: Purchase request approval record (item and budget)

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request
controls.decay_rationale: Human approval does not decay with model capability, but it is scoped to the budget/item decision only. It occurs before any vendor quote exists and its record is not passed to payments-agent, so it does not constrain the eventual choice of vendor or payment destination.

controls.name: Prompt instruction restricting payment to approved vendors
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced only by the model following 'Only pay vendors on the approved list.' Checks vendor identity but never validates bank account details, and a more capable or longer-running model can be misled by a quote that names an approved vendor but carries altered payment details.

controls.name: Signed/pinned agent card and mutual authentication for payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. If implemented, cryptographic identity verification would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Independent verification of payment bank details against vendor master record
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. As a structural check independent of quote-supplied content, this would sever the primary fraud path rather than merely narrow it.

controls.name: Propagate approval scope/context from the purchase request to payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. The approval record currently stays with the orchestrator and never reaches payments-agent.

controls.name: Anomaly detection and logging on payment tasks and bank-detail changes
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. A detective control would not prevent the payment but could enable faster clawback or review.

findings.title: Lethal-trifecta-style payment fraud (TC1 variant): untrusted vendor-quote bank details flow unchecked into an irreversible payment delegation

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled or compromised vendor email supplies bank account details
Orchestrator hands off a payment task using the quote's bank details, per prompt.md:3
Pays the supplied bank details with no independent verification

forecast.watch_signal: Model version upgraded for procurement-orchestrator, step/runtime limits raised or left unset, or vendor-list enforcement remaining purely in prompt text without an automated bank-detail check.

evidence.observation: 'Use the bank details from the chosen quote' — payment destination is taken directly from an externally sourced vendor quote.
'Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company' confirms quote content, including any bank details, is attacker-reachable.
'payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task' confirms no independent verification before payment.

recommendations.action: Verify payment bank/routing details against a vendor master record maintained independently of inbound quote emails; hold for manual review on any mismatch before invoking cap.delegate_payment.
Add a raw_action human approval gate immediately before payment execution, showing the actual bank account and amount, separate from the earlier budget approval.
Log and alert whenever quote-supplied bank details differ from the vendor's on-file payment details, even when the vendor name matches the approved list.

findings.title: Confused deputy via unverified peer identity (TC4): unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card and broad bearer token leave the payment delegation channel unverifiable

attack_path.note: Agent card fetched at startup, not signed or pinned; bearer token trusted for any task
Orchestrator delegates payment execution over this unverified channel

evidence.observation: authentication.schemes is ['bearer'] only; no mutual TLS or signed identity is used.
'The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned,' so identity cannot be verified across restarts or updates (rug-pull risk).
'payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task' — a single broadly trusted credential, not a per-request scoped authorization.

recommendations.action: Require signed, pinned agent cards and mutual TLS or signed identity for the A2A connection to payments-agent; reject unsigned/unpinned cards at startup.
Replace the standing bearer token with per-task, narrowly scoped credentials issued per payment request rather than a token trusted for any task.

findings.title: Authority laundering (TC7): budget approval predates vendor/bank-detail selection and its context never reaches payments-agent

attack_path.note: Manager approves item/budget before any vendor quote exists
Approval is scoped to budget/item only
Approval record is not passed to payments-agent
Final vendor and bank-detail choice happens later, unconstrained by the earlier approval
Executes payment from the delegated task alone, with no reference to the original approval scope

forecast.watch_signal: Autonomy level raised (e.g., toward A4) or the manager approval gate removed/narrowed, or vendor-allowlist enforcement dropped from the prompt without a structural replacement.

evidence.observation: 'The manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists. The approval record is not passed to payments-agent.'

'When a manager approves a purchase request, collect vendor quotes, choose the best one, and hand it to payments-agent to pay' — approval covers budget/item only, yet is the sole human checkpoint for the entire downstream payment.

recommendations.action: Propagate the approval record (budget, item, approving manager) with the delegated payment task, and require payments-agent to validate payment details against that propagated scope.
Add a second human checkpoint after vendor quote selection and before payment, not only at the initial budget request.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: untrusted vendor-quote email content (in.vendor_quote) directly determines the bank details passed into an S3 'delegate' payment action (cap.delegate_payment: irreversible, egress of confidential financial data), and no step or runtime limits are declared (F1). Residual risk stays critical because the A2A channel to payments-agent has no identity verification or definition pinning at all and relies on a single broadly trusted bearer token — no control in the design covers this path (F2), so residual equals inherent there. The one present control that does earn credit, a prompt instruction restricting payment to an approved vendor list, only reduces the direct fraud path (F1) from critical to high, and does not address bank-detail substitution within an otherwise-approved vendor's email, nor agent impersonation. Forecast risk remains critical: that sole behavioral control is dependent and is expected to fail under model_upgrade, longer_task_horizon, or autonomy_increase, returning F1 to critical, while F2 is already critical with nothing left to decay. The authority-laundering gap (F3) — a budget approval obtained before any vendor quote exists, whose scope never reaches payments-agent — explains structurally why the one existing human approval gate provides no credit against F1 or F2.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/A2A traffic captures, IaC, or payments-agent source/configuration were provided; payments-agent's internal controls are inferred solely from the runtime notes describing its behavior toward the orchestrator, so confidence there is medium even though the stated facts are explicit.

Autonomy level is inferred as A3 (act then report) from the absence of any stated post-action human review step for the payment delegation; no explicit reporting mechanism is described in the artifacts, which is itself a gap worth clarifying with the team.

No MCP config or tool manifest was supplied beyond the agent card; protocol-level auth classification (static_token) is inferred from the runtime notes' description of blanket trust rather than from a captured token scope.
